The given diagrams, I–IV, show four phases of mitosis in random order.

a. Describe the phase labelled as I. (2 marks)
b. Rearrange the phases of mitosis (I–IV) in sequence of their occurrence. (1 mark)

a. I is anaphase. Sister chromatids separate at their centromeres and move along spindle fibres towards opposite poles.
b. II → IV → I → III (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase).
Award two marks for describing anaphase and one for the complete sequence.

Describe the distribution of stomata and its advantages in hydrophytes and xerophytes.

| Feature | Hydrophytes | Xerophytes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distribution of stomata | … | … |
| Advantage | … | … |

Floating-leaved hydrophytes usually have stomata on the exposed upper surface, allowing exchange with the air. Fully submerged leaves may lack stomata. Many xerophytes have fewer, sunken or mainly lower-surface stomata. This limits exposure to dry moving air and reduces water loss.
For each plant group, credit one distribution feature and one linked advantage. The expected hydrophyte example is a floating leaf.

Observe the given diagram.

a. Identify joint X and describe its structure. (2 marks)
b. Describe the working of joint X while swimming. (1 mark)

a. X is the elbow hinge joint. The lower humerus articulates with the upper forearm bones, particularly the ulna at the hinge. Ligaments stabilise the joint.
b. The elbow bends and straightens in one plane, letting the swimmer pull and recover the arm.
Credit identification, one structural feature, and one point linking flexion or extension to the swimming movement.

Mr and Mrs Asad have brown eyes. They have five children, four of their children have brown eyes while one, Akram, has blue eyes. At the age of 30, Akram marries a woman who has brown (heterozygous) eyes. With reference to Akram and his wife, determine the possible genotypes and phenotypic ratio of Akram and his wife’s offspring through a genetic cross.

(Note: Represent the allele for brown and blue eye colour as B and b respectively.)

In the simplified model provided, Akram is bb and his wife is Bb. Akram’s gametes all carry b. His wife’s gametes carry B or b in equal proportions. The offspring genotypes are ½ Bb and ½ bb, for an expected 1 brown : 1 blue ratio. Real human eye colour involves multiple genes.
One mark each for the correct parental genotypes, offspring genotypes, and 1:1 expected phenotypic ratio.

Describe any TWO functions of each of the following parts of the human brain.

i. Thalamus (2 marks)
ii. Hypothalamus (2 marks)
iii. Cerebrum (2 marks)

i. The thalamus relays most sensory signals to the cortex and helps regulate alertness.
ii. The hypothalamus helps regulate body temperature and controls pituitary hormone release.
iii. The cerebrum initiates voluntary movements and supports higher functions such as reasoning and memory.
Two distinct functions per named part, one mark per function.

The given diagram shows different stages (I–VI) of seed germination.

i. Identify the given type of germination. (1 mark)
ii. Name any ONE seed that shows such type of germination. (1 mark)
iii. Describe any FOUR progressive changes from stages II to VI. (4 marks)

i. Epigeal germination.
ii. Bean.
iii. The radicle emerges and grows downwards. Lateral roots develop. The elongating hypocotyl lifts the cotyledons above the soil. The shoot straightens and the first foliage leaves open.
Credit the type, one valid seed example and four distinct changes tied to the pictured sequence.
6a

i. Explain how the survival of the fittest in a population leads to evolution. (4 marks)
ii. Bacteria have become resistant to antibiotics. Relate the given example with natural selection. (2 marks)

i. Individuals vary in heritable traits. Under selection pressure, those with traits that improve reproductive success tend to leave more offspring. These traits are inherited and become more common over generations. The population’s inherited composition changes.
ii. An antibiotic can inhibit susceptible bacteria while bacteria already carrying resistance are more likely to survive and reproduce. Resistance consequently becomes more common in the population.

Credit variation, differential survival or reproduction, inheritance, and change across generations. For the example, credit the contrast between susceptible and resistant bacteria and the resulting increase in resistance frequency.

Explain any THREE effects of each of the following environmental problems on the living organisms.

i. Global warming (3 marks)
ii. Urbanisation (3 marks)

i. Heat stress can reduce survival. A shift in suitable climate can force species to move or lose habitat. Changes in seasonal timing can separate pollinators from flowering plants.
ii. Construction removes habitat; roads fragment populations and reduce movement; urban pollution can impair organisms’ health and reproduction.
One mark per distinct and explained effect, up to three for each problem.
